exam_data <- read_csv("data/Exam_data.csv")

The dataset contains year-end examination grades of a cohort of Primary 3 students from a local school. It has seven attributes — four categorical (ID, CLASS, GENDER, RACE) and three continuous (MATHS, ENGLISH, SCIENCE).

title: Hands-on Exercise 1: A Layered Grammar of Graphics
text:
Bar Chart — geom_bar()
A bar chart showing the count of students by race.

The PlotThe Code














ggplot(data = exam_data,
       aes(x = RACE)) +
  geom_bar()

title: Hands-on Exercise 1: A Layered Grammar of Graphics
text:
Dot Plot — geom_dotplot()
A dot plot of Maths scores, where each dot represents one observation.

The PlotThe Code














ggplot(data = exam_data,
       aes(x = MATHS)) +
  geom_dotplot(binwidth = 2.5,
               dotsize = 0.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(NULL, breaks = NULL)

title: Hands-on Exercise 1: A Layered Grammar of Graphics
text:
Histogram — geom_histogram()
A histogram of Maths scores coloured by gender.

The PlotThe Code














ggplot(data = exam_data,
       aes(x = MATHS,
           fill = GENDER)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20,
                 color = "grey30")

title: Hands-on Exercise 1: A Layered Grammar of Graphics
text:
Kernel Density Estimate — geom_density()
A kernel density plot comparing Maths score distributions between genders.

ggplot(data = exam_data,

  geom_density()

title: Hands-on Exercise 1: A Layered Grammar of Graphics
text:
Box Plot — geom_boxplot()
A notched box plot of Maths scores by gender. Non-overlapping notches indicate differing medians.

       aes(y = MATHS,
           x = GENDER)) +
  geom_boxplot(notch = TRUE)

text:

ggplot(data = exam_data,

           x = GENDER)) +

title: Hands-on Exercise 1: A Layered Grammar of Graphics

title: Hands-on Exercise 1: A Layered Grammar of Graphics

Adding Mean Points — stat_summary()

title: Hands-on Exercise 2
text:
Beyond ggplot2 Annotation: ggrepel

Without ggrepel

The PlotThe Code














ggplot(exam_data, aes(x = MATHS, y = ENGLISH)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text(aes(label = ID), hjust = 0.5, vjust = -0.5) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0,100), ylim = c(0,100)) +
  ggtitle("English vs Maths scores - without ggrepel")






With ggrepel

The PlotThe Code














ggplot(exam_data, aes(x = MATHS, y = ENGLISH)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = ID), size = 3) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0,100), ylim = c(0,100)) +
  ggtitle("English vs Maths scores - with ggrepel")

title: Hands-on Exercise 2
text:
Beyond ggplot2 Themes

ggthemes — Economist theme

The PlotThe Code














ggplot(exam_data, aes(x = MATHS)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "grey", color = "black") +
  ggtitle("Distribution of Maths scores") +
  theme_economist()






hrbrthemes

The PlotThe Code

  geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "grey", color = "black") +
  ggtitle("Distribution of Maths scores") +
  theme_ipsum(axis_title_size = 18, base_size = 15, grid = "Y")

title: Hands-on Exercise 2
text:
Beyond Single Graph: patchwork

Two graphs side by side

The PlotThe Code














p1 <- ggplot(exam_data, aes(x = MATHS)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, color = "grey30", fill = "grey90") +
  ggtitle("Distribution of Maths scores")

p2 <- ggplot(exam_data, aes(x = ENGLISH)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, color = "grey30", fill = "grey90") +
  ggtitle("Distribution of English scores")

p1 + p2






Three graphs combined

The PlotThe Code














p3 <- ggplot(exam_data, aes(x = MATHS, y = ENGLISH)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = lm, linewidth = 0.5) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0,100), ylim = c(0,100)) +
  ggtitle("English vs Maths scores")

(p1 / p2) | p3






With auto-tagging

The PlotThe Code














((p1 / p2) | p3) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = 'I')






Inset plot

The PlotThe Code














p3 + inset_element(p2, left = 0.02, bottom = 0.7, right = 0.5, top = 1)

title: Hands-on Exercise 4
text:
pacman::p_load(ggdist, ggridges, ggthemes,
               colorspace, tidyverse)





exam <- read_csv("data/Exam_data.csv")








The PlotThe Code














ggplot(exam, 
       aes(x = ENGLISH, 
           y = CLASS)) +
  geom_density_ridges(
    scale = 3,
    rel_min_height = 0.01,
    bandwidth = 3.4,
    fill = lighten("#7097BB", .3),
    color = "white"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    name = "English grades",
    expand = c(0, 0)
    ) +
  scale_y_discrete(name = NULL, expand = expansion(add = c(0.2, 2.6))) +
  theme_ridges()








The PlotThe Code














ggplot(exam, 
       aes(x = ENGLISH, 
           y = CLASS,
           fill = stat(x))) +
  geom_density_ridges_gradient(
    scale = 3,
    rel_min_height = 0.01) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Temp. [F]",
                       option = "C") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    name = "English grades",
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(name = NULL, expand = expansion(add = c(0.2, 2.6))) +
  theme_ridges()








The PlotThe Code














ggplot(exam,
       aes(x = ENGLISH, 
           y = CLASS, 
           fill = 0.5 - abs(0.5-stat(ecdf)))) +
  stat_density_ridges(geom = "density_ridges_gradient", 
                      calc_ecdf = TRUE) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Tail probability",
                       direction = -1) +
  theme_ridges()








The PlotThe Code














ggplot(exam,
       aes(x = ENGLISH, 
           y = CLASS, 
           fill = factor(stat(quantile))
           )) +
  stat_density_ridges(
    geom = "density_ridges_gradient",
    calc_ecdf = TRUE, 
    quantiles = 4,
    quantile_lines = TRUE) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(name = "Quartiles") +
  theme_ridges()








The PlotThe Code














ggplot(exam,
       aes(x = ENGLISH, 
           y = CLASS, 
           fill = factor(stat(quantile))
           )) +
  stat_density_ridges(
    geom = "density_ridges_gradient",
    calc_ecdf = TRUE, 
    quantiles = c(0.025, 0.975)
    ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Probability",
    values = c("#FF0000A0", "#A0A0A0A0", "#0000FFA0"),
    labels = c("(0, 0.025]", "(0.025, 0.975]", "(0.975, 1]")
  ) +
  theme_ridges()











The PlotThe Code














ggplot(exam, 
       aes(x = RACE, 
           y = ENGLISH)) +
  stat_halfeye(adjust = 0.5,
               justification = -0.2,
               .width = 0,
               point_colour = NA)








The PlotThe Code














ggplot(exam, 
       aes(x = RACE, 
           y = ENGLISH)) +
  stat_halfeye(adjust = 0.5,
               justification = -0.2,
               .width = 0,
               point_colour = NA) +
  geom_boxplot(width = .20,
               outlier.shape = NA)








The PlotThe Code














ggplot(exam, 
       aes(x = RACE, 
           y = ENGLISH)) +
  stat_halfeye(adjust = 0.5,
               justification = -0.2,
               .width = 0,
               point_colour = NA) +
  geom_boxplot(width = .20,
               outlier.shape = NA) +
  stat_dots(side = "left", 
            justification = 1.2, 
            binwidth = .5,
            dotsize = 2)








The PlotThe Code














ggplot(exam, 
       aes(x = RACE, 
           y = ENGLISH)) +
  stat_halfeye(adjust = 0.5,
               justification = -0.2,
               .width = 0,
               point_colour = NA) +
  geom_boxplot(width = .20,
               outlier.shape = NA) +
  stat_dots(side = "left", 
            justification = 1.2, 
            binwidth = .5,
            dotsize = 1.5) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_economist()

title: Hands-on Exercise 4
text:
Visualising Uncertainty with ggplot2

Computing Summary Statistics

my_sum <- exam %>%
  group_by(RACE) %>%
  summarise(
    n=n(),
    mean=mean(MATHS),
    sd=sd(MATHS)
    ) %>%
  mutate(se=sd/sqrt(n-1))



Standard Error Bars

The PlotThe Code














ggplot(my_sum) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(x=RACE, 
        ymin=mean-se, 
        ymax=mean+se), 
    width=0.2, 
    colour="black", 
    alpha=0.9, 
    linewidth=0.5) +
  geom_point(aes(x=RACE, 
                 y=mean), 
             stat="identity", 
             color="red",
             size = 1.5,
             alpha=1) +
  ggtitle("Standard error of mean maths score by race")






95% Confidence Interval

The PlotThe Code














ggplot(my_sum) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(x=reorder(RACE, -mean), 
        ymin=mean-1.96*se, 
        ymax=mean+1.96*se), 
    width=0.2, 
    colour="black", 
    alpha=0.9, 
    linewidth=0.5) +
  geom_point(aes(x=RACE, 
                 y=mean), 
             stat="identity", 
             color="red",
             size = 1.5,
             alpha=1) +
  labs(x = "Maths score",
       title = "95% confidence interval of mean maths score by race")






Interactive Error Bars: 99% Confidence Interval

The PlotThe Code





















shared_df = SharedData$new(my_sum)

bscols(widths = c(4,8),
       ggplotly((ggplot(shared_df) +
                   geom_errorbar(aes(
                     x=reorder(RACE, -mean),
                     ymin=mean-2.58*se, 
                     ymax=mean+2.58*se), 
                     width=0.2, 
                     colour="black", 
                     alpha=0.9, 
                     size=0.5) +
                   geom_point(aes(
                     x=RACE, 
                     y=mean, 
                     text = paste("Race:", `RACE`, 
                                  "<br>N:", `n`,
                                  "<br>Avg. Scores:", round(mean, digits = 2),
                                  "<br>95% CI:[", 
                                  round((mean-2.58*se), digits = 2), ",",
                                  round((mean+2.58*se), digits = 2),"]")),
                     stat="identity", 
                     color="red", 
                     size = 1.5, 
                     alpha=1) + 
                   xlab("Race") + 
                   ylab("Average Scores") + 
                   theme_minimal() + 
                   theme(axis.text.x = element_text(
                     angle = 45, vjust = 0.5, hjust=1)) +
                   ggtitle("99% Confidence interval of average maths scores by race")), 
                tooltip = "text"), 
       DT::datatable(shared_df, 
                     rownames = FALSE, 
                     class="compact", 
                     width="100%", 
                     options = list(pageLength = 10,
                                    scrollX=T), 
                     colnames = c("No. of pupils", 
                                  "Avg Scores",
                                  "Std Dev",
                                  "Std Error")) %>%
         formatRound(columns=c('mean', 'sd', 'se'),
                     digits=2))

A funnel plot object with 267 points of which 0 are outliers. 
Plot is adjusted for overdispersion.

  denominator = Death,

)

  numerator = Death,
  denominator = Positive,
  group = `Sub-district`,
  data_type = "PR",

  yrange = c(0, 0.05)
)






Makeover 2: Adding Labels and Title

The PlotThe Code











A funnel plot object with 267 points of which 7 are outliers. 
Plot is adjusted for overdispersion.

  .data = covid19,
  numerator = Death,
  denominator = Positive,
  group = `Sub-district`,
  data_type = "PR",

title: Hands-on Exercise 4
text:
Funnel Plot with ggplot2

Computing Derived Fields

df <- covid19 %>%
  mutate(rate = Death / Positive) %>%
  mutate(rate.se = sqrt((rate*(1-rate)) / (Positive))) %>%
  filter(rate > 0)

fit.mean <- weighted.mean(df$rate, 1/df$rate.se^2)



Computing Confidence Interval Limits

number.seq <- seq(1, max(df$Positive), 1)
number.ll95 <- fit.mean - 1.96 * sqrt((fit.mean*(1-fit.mean)) / (number.seq)) 
number.ul95 <- fit.mean + 1.96 * sqrt((fit.mean*(1-fit.mean)) / (number.seq)) 
number.ll999 <- fit.mean - 3.29 * sqrt((fit.mean*(1-fit.mean)) / (number.seq)) 
number.ul999 <- fit.mean + 3.29 * sqrt((fit.mean*(1-fit.mean)) / (number.seq)) 
dfCI <- data.frame(number.ll95, number.ul95, number.ll999, 
                   number.ul999, number.seq, fit.mean)



Static Funnel Plot

The PlotThe Code

  geom_point(aes(label=`Sub-district`), 
             alpha=0.4) +
  geom_line(data = dfCI, 
            aes(x = number.seq, y = number.ll95), 
            size = 0.4, colour = "grey40", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(data = dfCI, 
            aes(x = number.seq, y = number.ul95), 
            size = 0.4, colour = "grey40", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(data = dfCI, 
            aes(x = number.seq, y = number.ll999), 
            size = 0.4, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_line(data = dfCI, 
            aes(x = number.seq, y = number.ul999), 
            size = 0.4, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_hline(data = dfCI, 
             aes(yintercept = fit.mean), 
             size = 0.4, colour = "grey40") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim=c(0,0.05)) +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = -0.13, label = "95%", size = 3, colour = "grey40") + 
  annotate("text", x = 4.5, y = -0.18, label = "99%", size = 3, colour = "grey40") + 
  ggtitle("Cumulative Fatality Rate by Cumulative Number of COVID-19 Cases") +
  xlab("Cumulative Number of COVID-19 Cases") + 
  ylab("Cumulative Fatality Rate") +
  theme_light() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size=12),

        legend.text = element_text(size=7),

With Correlation Coefficients

The PlotThe Code














panel.cor <- function(x, y, digits=2, prefix="", cex.cor, ...) {
  usr <- par("usr")
  on.exit(par(usr))
  par(usr = c(0, 1, 0, 1))
  r <- abs(cor(x, y, use="complete.obs"))
  txt <- format(c(r, 0.123456789), digits=digits)[1]
  txt <- paste(prefix, txt, sep="")
  if(missing(cex.cor)) cex.cor <- 0.8/strwidth(txt)
  text(0.5, 0.5, txt, cex = cex.cor * (1 + r) / 2)
}

pairs(wine[,2:12],
      upper.panel = panel.cor)

Importing Data

realis2018 <- read_csv("data/realis2018.csv")

title: Hands-on Exercise 5
text:
Data Wrangling

Grouped Summaries with Pipe

realis2018_summarised <- realis2018 %>%
  group_by(`Project Name`,`Planning Region`,
           `Planning Area`, `Property Type`,
           `Type of Sale`) %>%
  summarise(`Total Unit Sold` = sum(`No. of Units`, na.rm = TRUE),
            `Total Area` = sum(`Area (sqm)`, na.rm = TRUE),
            `Median Unit Price ($ psm)` = median(`Unit Price ($ psm)`, na.rm = TRUE),
            `Median Transacted Price` = median(`Transacted Price ($)`, na.rm = TRUE))



Filtering Resale Condominiums

realis2018_selected <- realis2018_summarised %>%
  filter(`Property Type` == "Condominium", `Type of Sale` == "Resale")

title: Hands-on Exercise 5

title: Hands-on Exercise 5
text:
Designing Treemap using treemapify Package

Basic treemapify

The PlotThe Code














ggplot(data=realis2018_selected,
       aes(area = `Total Unit Sold`,
           fill = `Median Unit Price ($ psm)`),
       layout = "scol",
       start = "bottomleft") +
  geom_treemap() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "light blue", high = "blue")






Group by Planning Region

The PlotThe Code














ggplot(data=realis2018_selected,
       aes(area = `Total Unit Sold`,
           fill = `Median Unit Price ($ psm)`,
           subgroup = `Planning Region`),
       start = "topleft") +
  geom_treemap()






Group by Planning Area with Boundary Lines

The PlotThe Code














ggplot(data=realis2018_selected,
       aes(area = `Total Unit Sold`,
           fill = `Median Unit Price ($ psm)`,
           subgroup = `Planning Region`,
           subgroup2 = `Planning Area`)) +
  geom_treemap() +
  geom_treemap_subgroup2_border(colour = "gray40",
                                size = 2) +
  geom_treemap_subgroup_border(colour = "gray20")

title: Hands-on Exercise 5
text:
Designing Interactive Treemap using d3treeR

Installing d3treeR

library(devtools)
install_github("timelyportfolio/d3treeR")



Interactive Treemap

The PlotThe Code

























library(d3treeR)

tm <- treemap(realis2018_summarised,
        index=c("Planning Region", "Planning Area"),
        vSize="Total Unit Sold",
        vColor="Median Unit Price ($ psm)",
        type="value",
        title="Private Residential Property Sold, 2017",
        title.legend = "Median Unit Price (S$ per sq. m)"
        )

d3tree(tm, rootname = "Singapore")
